title: 48-byte range copy with retain
summary: VA 0x4b3eb0 advances source and destination in 48-byte steps, copying each non-null destination using the retain helper. The original internal calling convention uses ECX and EDX for bounds and a caller-cleaned stack destination; the portable source exposes the same semantics with a normal C++ interface.
test_description: Direct comparison against both linked accepted originals over empty and one-to-three element ranges, all nullable-pointer masks, shared and distinct resources, reference-count wraparound, self-copy and overlapping ranges. Whole-arena comparisons cover guards, source, overwritten destination and resource side effects. Invalid pointers test empty and null-destination one-element paths; FS head is checked after original calls.
known_limits: The recovered interface is a semantic adapter, not the original internal register/stack ABI.
The test oracle's GCC fastcall declaration assumes callee cleanup; a noinline frame-backed adapter restores the caller-cleaned stack argument under the fixed O0 build flags.
Ranges must reach the end by repeated 48-byte increments; other cases do not terminate normally. Null destination is only safe for a single skipped element unless later addresses are valid.
Reference ownership types and payload field meanings remain unresolved; increments are non-atomic and overwritten destination references are not released.
No exception or invalid-memory behavior is modeled.
